goal_summary: Let a user move an existing integration (notably the singleton MS Teams one) to another project from the UI, safely handling dependents and permissions; works when the integration lands in the target project, is gone from the source and its dependents fail visibly.

integrations with external systems.reason: MS Teams bot feature flag is a stand constraint; no external call is made by the change

open_questions.question: Must the project change go through POST /v1/settings/transfer from the UI, or is a PUT whose server side calls the transfer service acceptable?

source_says.quote: The UI must invoke the transfer endpoint instead
update_project_setting calls SettingsTransferService.transfer_setting; UI has no settings/transfer call

readings.reading: Transfer endpoint is required; the delivered PUT path is a defect
readings.if_chosen: R-3 oracle is the endpoint call; a UI test asserting the request URL; PUT path logged as APP_BUG

readings.reading: Server-side PUT with in-transaction transfer is acceptable
readings.if_chosen: R-3 is checked by outcome (project moved, dependents handled), not by URL

open_questions.question: Must Move succeed for an MS Teams integration (budget-switch scenario)?

source_says.quote: Move mode is valid for MS Teams and should be available through the UI
ms_teams PUT with different project_name raises 400 Project mismatch

readings.reading: Move must succeed for MS Teams; the 400 is a defect
readings.if_chosen: R-5 expects a moved integration; the current rejection is filed as APP_BUG

readings.reading: MS Teams cannot change project through the edit form; only the transfer endpoint moves it
readings.if_chosen: R-5 is checked on the transfer endpoint only and the UI edit path expects the 400

open_questions.question: Must the UI let the user choose between move and copy, and is copy in scope?

source_says.quote: explicitly choose the applicable transfer mode
no mode selector in diff; only a confirm modal

readings.reading: Both modes are required in the UI
readings.if_chosen: R-4 gets move and copy cases; the missing selector is a defect
copy cases are dropped, R-4 reduced to target project selection

open_questions.question: Is editing the Project of an existing integration a feature or the designed behaviour it was called earlier?

source_says.quote: it's not a defect - it's expected behaviour. It was designed like this
Recommend keeping open as a focused contributor candidate

readings.reading: Feature is wanted, later comments supersede
Project must stay locked on edit
readings.if_chosen: R-1 and R-2 become negative checks

open_questions.question: Are the behaviours that only the diff speaks to (atomic update+move, datasource unlink, target-project admin check, confirm modal, user-scope PUT move, credential-type reset skip) the intended behaviour?

source_says.quote: user-scope PUT also moves project via transfer_setting in one transaction
on MOVE, datasources left in source project have IndexInfo.setting_id cleared

readings.if_chosen: R-11..R-16 become confirmed rows; checks assert the as-built outcome

readings.reading: The behaviour before is expected (a regression)
readings.if_chosen: the affected rows are filed as APP_BUG

before.value: project not editable; each write in its own session

now.value: project editable; one transaction; datasource links cleared; confirm modal

open_questions.question: After a transfer, which lists and state must refresh for source and target, and where is this observable?

source_says.quote: refresh the integration list and project-scoped data for both source and target projects
refresh not shown in diff hunks

readings.reading: Refresh after performUpdate is sufficient and checked in the UI
readings.if_chosen: R-9 gets a UI check of both project lists

readings.reading: Separate explicit refresh of project-scoped data is required
readings.if_chosen: R-9 stays a manual row until an observable is named
